title: pika: A lightweight package for evaluating correlation between time series
text: estimate effective reproduction number (Rt), pika function estimate_rt() provides wrapper EpiEstim::estimate_R() [3] enables users estimate Rt grouping variable. input estimate_rt() takes data frame daily cases deaths group. pika includes example data set china_case_data.rda includes daily reported cases COVID-19 several provinces China 16 January 2020 24 March 2020. estimate Rt case data, user must specify data set dat = argument estimate_rt(). data set include three columns: date column (class ‘date’), grouping variable, value used estimate Rt (commonly cases, quantities can used, deaths). names columns input data set specified character strings grp_var =, date_var =, incidence_var = arguments. method used estimate Rt can changed using est_method = argument. argument takes following options: c("non_parametric_si","parametric_si","uncertain_si","si_from_data","si_from_sample"). methods require specifying mean standard deviation serial interval, parameters can set using si_mean = si_std = function arguments. default values si_mean = 6.48 si_std = 3.83 [4]. information methodology underlying EpiEstim::estimate_R look vignette help("estimate_R").
code: # to estimate them with pika, use estimate_rt() ------------------------------------------ rt_estimates <- estimate_rt(dat = china_case_data,                             grp_var = "province",                             date_var = "date",                             incidence_var = "cases"                             ) %>%   # a little data formatting--------------------------------------------------------------   mutate(province = to_snake_case(province)) %>%   select(-date_start) %>%   rename("date" = "date_end")

title: pika: A lightweight package for evaluating correlation between time series
text: determining relationship two time series sometimes interest determine lag correlation two time series highest, ’ll call optimal lag. determine optimal lag, two time series must first merged single data frame. using dplyr’s left_join() date province. can identify optimal lag calculating cross correlation two time series grouping variable different lags using cross_corr function. argument max_lag = specifies maximum lag test. example set 10 days. subset_date = argument allows user determine cross correlation two time series subset time window. optimal lag determined, must back date Rt estimates without impacting date movement variable.
code: # Join data sets together by date and province to determine cross correlation ----------- # for this we are using input rt estimates, not those estimated using pika::estimate_rt() data_joined <- left_join(rt_estimates,                          exante_movement_data,                          by = c("date","province")                          ) # # Determine lag with max cross correlation between Rt and movement ---------------------- lags <- cross_corr(dat = data_joined,                    date_var = "date",                    grp_var = "province",                    x_var = "r_mean",                    y_var = "movement",                    max_lag = 10,                    subset_date = "2020-02-15"                   )  # use min lag across groups ------------------------------------------------------------- my_lag <- min(lags$lag) # create lag date using max lag from cross_corr() --------------------------------------- data_joined_lag <- rt_estimates %>%   mutate(date = date + my_lag) %>%   left_join(., exante_movement_data, by = c("date", "province"))

title: pika: A lightweight package for evaluating correlation between time series
text: often interest determine relationship two time series, specifically rolling correlation. rolling_corr() function calculates rolling correlation two times series (x_var y_var) specified time window n =. , calculate biweekly rolling correlation Rt movement. Since data daily estimates Rt movement, set n = 14. data monthly wanted determine 6 month rolling correlation, set n = 6. output rolling_corr() data frame additional column added input dataset called “rolling_corr”. Depending value n, first n values “rolling_corr” NA. visualise rolling correlation, results rolling_corr() can plotted using plot_corr(). creates plot two time series rolling correlation facetted grouping variable. optional arguments change facet labels (facet_lables =), legend_labels (legend_labels =), add confidence bounds primary time series (x_var_lower = x_var_upper =), set maximum value y-axis (y_max =). code plots mean Rt estimates 95% confidence bands, movement index, biweekly correlation . also specify custom facet legend labels restrict y-axis maximum value 10.
code: # Determine rolling correlation between Rt and movement --------------------------------- data_corr <- rolling_corr(dat = data_joined_lag,                           date_var = "date",                           grp_var = "province",                           x_var = "r_mean",                           y_var = "movement",                           n = 14) # Plot Rt, movement, and correlation ---------------------------------------------------- my_labels <- c("beijing" = "Beijing", "guangdong" = "Guangdong", "henan" = "Henan",                "hong_kong_sar" = "Hong Kong SAR", "hubei" = "Hubei", "hunan" = "Hunan",                "zhejiang" = "Zhejiang") my_legend = c("Correlation", "Reproduction Number", "Movement")  plot_corr(dat = data_corr,           date_var = "date",           grp_var = "province",           x_var = "r_mean",           y_var = "movement",           x_var_lower = "r_q2.5",           x_var_upper = "r_q97.5",           facet_labels = my_labels,           legend_labels = my_legend,           y_max = 10           )

code: library(pika)  # Load example data data(china_case_data) data(exante_movement_data)  # Estimate reproduction number by province rt_estimates <- estimate_rt(   dat = china_case_data,   grp_var = "province",   date_var = "date",   incidence_var = "cases" )  # Join Rt estimates with mobility data data_joined <- dplyr::left_join(   rt_estimates,   exante_movement_data,   by = c("date_end" = "date", "province") )  # Determine optimal lag between Rt and movement lags <- cross_corr(   dat = data_joined,   date_var = "date_end",   grp_var = "province",   x_var = "r_mean",   y_var = "movement",   max_lag = 10 )  # Calculate rolling correlation data_corr <- rolling_corr(   dat = data_joined,   date_var = "date_end",   grp_var = "province",   x_var = "r_mean",   y_var = "movement",   n = 14 )  # Visualize results plot_corr(   dat = data_corr,   date_var = "date_end",   grp_var = "province",   x_var = "r_mean",   y_var = "movement" )

title: Convert a count time series to fractional change relative to a baseline period — calc_percent_change
text: dat data frame containing count column, date column, grouping column. date_var Character string giving name date column (class Date). Default "date". grp_var Character string giving name grouping column. baseline mean computed separately per group. count_var Character string giving name count column. n_baseline_periods Integer. Number consecutive time steps used compute baseline mean. daily data, 7 gives one-week baseline. Default 7. start_date Start date baseline period. Accepts Date object character string "YYYY-MM-DD" format (e.g. "2020-01-13"). NULL (default), earliest date across combined dataset used baseline start.

title: Convert a count time series to fractional change relative to a baseline period — calc_percent_change
text: input data frame one additional numeric column,   perc_change, giving observation fractional change   relative group-specific baseline mean (0 = change   baseline, -1 = zero counts, positive values = baseline).

title: Convert a count time series to fractional change relative to a baseline period — calc_percent_change
text: $$\texttt{perc\_change} = \frac{\texttt{count} -   \texttt{baseline mean}}{\texttt{baseline mean}}$$ value 0 indicates change baseline; -0.5 indicates 50% decrease; 1.0 indicates doubling. Originally developed population mobility data applicable non-negative count series.

what: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr
title: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr
text: Computes cross-correlation function (CCF) x_var y_var lags -max_lag 0 using ccf, returns lag highest CCF group. non-positive lags considered (.e. x_var leading y_var), reflecting assumption changes primary series precede changes secondary series.

title: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr
code: cross_corr(   dat,   date_var = NULL,   grp_var,   x_var,   y_var,   max_lag = 20,   subset_date = NULL )

title: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr
text: dat data frame containing two time series grouping column. date_var Character string giving name date column. Required subset_date non-NULL. supplied, rows sorted date_var within group CCF computed (required ccf assumes row order chronological). NULL, dat must already sorted chronologically within group. grp_var Character string giving name grouping column. CCF computed separately within group. x_var Character string giving name primary (leading) time series column. y_var Character string giving name secondary (lagged) time series column. max_lag Integer. Maximum number lags evaluate. CCF computed lags -max_lag 0. Default 20. subset_date Character string format date_var. supplied, rows dates subset_date used. Requires date_var specified.

title: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr
text: tibble one row per group containing: <grp_var> Group identifier; column name matches grp_var. lag Integer \(\leq 0\). lag CCF       x_var y_var highest within group.

title: Find the lag at which cross-correlation between two time series is maximised — cross_corr

what: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
title: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
text: grouped wrapper around estimate_R (Cori et al. 2013). group, Rt estimated sliding weekly window using Bayesian framework Gamma-distributed serial interval. Results groups combined single data frame.

title: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
code: estimate_rt(   dat,   grp_var,   date_var,   incidence_var,   est_method = "parametric_si",   si_mean = 6.48,   si_std = 3.83 )

title: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
text: dat data frame least date column, incidence column, grouping column. NA values permitted incidence_var. grp_var Character string giving name grouping column. Rt estimated independently group. date_var Character string giving name date column. incidence_var Character string giving name daily incidence (case count) column. est_method Character string specifying serial interval estimation method passed estimate_R. One "parametric_si" (default), "non_parametric_si", "uncertain_si", "si_from_data", "si_from_sample". si_mean Mean serial interval distribution (days). Used est_method = "parametric_si". Default 6.48 (COVID-19; Nishiura et al. 2020). si_std Standard deviation serial interval distribution (days). Used est_method = "parametric_si". Default 3.83 (COVID-19; Nishiura et al. 2020).

title: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
text: data frame one row per estimation window per group, containing: date_start Start date estimation window. date_end End date estimation window. <grp_var> Group identifier; column name matches grp_var. r_mean Posterior mean Rt. r_median Posterior median Rt. r_q2.5 2.5th percentile posterior (lower 95% credible interval). r_q97.5 97.5th percentile posterior (upper 95% credible interval).

title: Estimate the effective reproduction number (Rt) over time by group — estimate_rt
text: default serial interval parameters (si_mean = 6.48, si_std = 3.83) Nishiura et al. (2020) COVID-19 updated pathogens.

what: Plot time series and rolling correlation over time by group — plot_corr
title: Plot time series and rolling correlation over time by group — plot_corr
text: Produces faceted line plot showing primary series (x_var), secondary series (y_var), rolling correlation (roll_corr) time, one facet per group. Horizontal reference lines drawn y = -1 (dashed), 0 (solid), 1 (dashed). Optionally adds shaded confidence ribbon around x_var. dat contains column named roll_corr (e.g. rolling_corr) included plot; absent line simply omitted.

title: Plot time series and rolling correlation over time by group — plot_corr
code: plot_corr(   dat,   date_var,   grp_var,   x_var,   y_var,   x_var_lower = NULL,   x_var_upper = NULL,   facet_labels = NULL,   legend_labels = NULL,   y_max = NULL,   col_values = c(brewer.pal(8, "RdPu")[8], brewer.pal(8, "Greens")[5], brewer.pal(8,     "Blues")[8]) )

title: Plot time series and rolling correlation over time by group — plot_corr
text: dat data frame containing two time series, roll_corr column, date column, grouping column. date_var Character string giving name date column (class Date). grp_var Character string giving name grouping column used faceting. x_var Character string giving name primary time series column. y_var Character string giving name secondary time series column. x_var_lower Character string giving name column containing lower confidence bound x_var. NULL (default), ribbon drawn. x_var_lower x_var_upper must supplied draw ribbon. x_var_upper Character string giving name column containing upper confidence bound x_var. NULL (default), ribbon drawn. facet_labels Named character vector display labels facets, passed as_labeller. Names must match values grouping column. NULL (default), raw group values shown. legend_labels Character vector length 3 giving legend labels roll_corr, x_var, y_var respectively. NULL (default), internal metric names (roll_corr, x_var, y_var) shown legend. y_max Numeric. Maximum value y-axis. supplied, axis set [-1, y_max] confidence bounds clamped value. Default NULL (auto-scaled). col_values Character vector length 3 specifying line colours roll_corr, x_var, y_var respectively. Defaults dark purple, mid-green, dark blue RColorBrewer palettes.

what: Calculate rolling (moving-window) correlation between two time series — rolling_corr
title: Calculate rolling (moving-window) correlation between two time series — rolling_corr

Rows sorted date_var within group rolling correlation computed (required runCor assumes row order chronological). grp_var Character string giving name grouping column. Rolling correlation computed separately within group. x_var Character string giving name primary time series column. y_var Character string giving name secondary time series column. n Integer. Width rolling window time periods. Default 14.

title: Calculate rolling (moving-window) correlation between two time series — rolling_corr
text: data frame columns input plus one additional   numeric column, roll_corr, containing rolling Pearson   correlation x_var y_var. Values range -1   1. first n - 1 observations per group NA.
